name: Henry S. Boice
role: Manager, Berry Boice Land & Cattle Co. (777); stockgrowers' association officer
bio: Henry S. Boice was a cattleman of Berry, Boice & Co., also called the Berry Boice Land & Cattle Co. or the 777 outfit, managed from Mingusville, Montana, with a range on Beaver Creek. In March 1884 he and Towers arranged a round-up meeting at Little Missouri, and from December 1884 he was vice-chairman of the Little Missouri River Stockmen's Association under Theodore Roosevelt, re-elected in September 1885. In summer 1885 he brought 777 cattle to Medora and delivered five hundred head, and in 1886 he chaired a Mingusville meeting, was recommended by the association as one of Dakota's members of the executive committee at the Miles City meeting, scouted ranges in the Northwest Territory, and in August was elected the association's chairman. That September he shipped about 400 mares and colts to the 777's Beaver Creek range to raise the company's cow-horses.
